analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 10.1.26
key_insights: Futures bid early (Nasdaq +65bps, S&P +25bps) despite WTI up 2% and the 10-year yield above 5.30%, the first time since 2002. Macro news was quiet overnight and the focus was on earnings and AI developments.
Micron (MU) is down 1% pre-market, oscillating around flat, despite a quarter and guidance GS thinks should be good enough to sustain optimism in memory and the broader AI infrastructure trade.

Micron reported revenue of $54.23 bn vs GS $51.91 bn and Street $50.95 bn. Non-GAAP EPS was $33.42 vs GS $32.54 and Street $31.63. Gross margin of 87.0% was just below GS at 87.3% and in line with the Street at 86.9%.

Micron has signed 26 strategic customer agreements, up from 16 last quarter. They are generally five-year take-or-pay agreements with $32bn in up-front customer deposits so far. About 75% now contain structured pricing, and committed revenue is about $150bn over five years at floor prices.

Micron signed agreements cover about 35% of anticipated revenue through FY30, and management expects to cover about 50% over time. The agreements include four very large customers (two hyperscalers) and three medium-sized customers.

Micron FY1Q guidance: revenue midpoint of $61.5 bn vs GS $57.70 bn and Street $57.57 bn. Non-GAAP gross margin of 86.25% is below GS at 88.1% and the Street at 87.4%, because higher-cost inventory is expected to be sold, an effect that should partly abate in FY2Q. EPS guidance midpoint of $38.15 compares with GS $37.06 and Street $35.81.
Accenture (ACN) is up 17% pre-market, which would be its largest one-day gain on record, after a beat across the board against very bearish expectations. CTSH is up 8% and IBM up 6% in sympathy.

Accenture 4Q26 revenue was $18.68 bn vs Street $18.04 bn and GS $18.13 bn. EPS from continuing operations was $3.29 vs Street $3.19 and GS $3.12. Adjusted operating margin was 15.3% vs 15.2% expected. New bookings were $22.7 bn vs Street $19.90 bn.

Accenture FY27 guidance: constant-currency revenue growth of 3-6% ($76.4-78.6 bn) vs GS 3.0-4.0% and Street $76.4 bn. Operating margin expansion is guided at 10-30 bps. Adjusted EPS is guided at $14.39-14.81 vs Street $14.62, free cash flow at $11.9-12.7 bn, with about $9.5 bn to be returned to shareholders. Investor Day is Oct 14.
Accenture 1Q27 guidance is 2-6% constant-currency revenue growth with a negative 1% FX impact, or $18.95-19.60 bn, vs Street and GS at $19.4 bn.

Synopsys (SNPS) is up 3.5% on better guidance and follow-through from its analyst day. GS (Buy) cites long-term targets of about 15% revenue CAGR for FY26-30, 50% operating margin in FY30 and EPS of $35.00 in FY30, all above the Street. It also cites AI monetization including an OpenAI partnership, and a Design IP roadmap.

Alphabet (GOOGL) is up 2% after announcing Gemini 4 Argon, rolling it out first to the US government and trusted cybersecurity partners. This follows a roughly 2% sell-off into Wednesday's close on reports of internal skepticism about model performance. Google says the model sets a record in software engineering and ties for first in cybersecurity.
Tencent leased about 100,000 advanced AI chips from Oracle (ORCL) in south-east Asia under a five-year deal worth about $7bn, with about 30% paid upfront (FT).

France unveiled a €54 billion fiscal consolidation plan targeting a 5% of GDP deficit in 2027, down from 5.4%. The OAT-Bund spread widened to 134bps intraday, the widest since 2012, then retraced to about 129bps after the auction.

GS October US Conviction List adds Amazon (AMZN), Burlington Stores (BURL), Huntington Ingalls (HII), Johnson Controls (JCI) and Occidental Petroleum (OXY). It removes Air Products (APD), ConocoPhillips (COP), Golar LNG (GLNG), Loar Holdings (LOAR) and Tyson Foods (TSN).

GS reiterates Buy on Samsung Electronics (W490,000 TP) and cuts its 3Q26E operating profit estimate by 5% to W106tn on a stronger KRW. It expects 2027 HBM revenue above W100tn and 2027-28 estimates 8-17% above the Street. The stock trades at 3.6x P/E and 1.6x P/B on 2027E.

TrendForce forecasts 4Q26 DRAM ASP for PC/server/mobile at +13-18%/+10-15%/+0-5% qoq and NAND ASP at +15-20% qoq. These are above GS for PC DRAM, server DRAM and NAND, and in line for mobile DRAM. GS reiterates Buy on Samsung and SK Hynix.

The GS DRAM Sentiment Indicator for September 2026 is moderately positive, same as August. DDR5/DDR4 pricing is still rising, Taiwan server ODM monthly revenue is up a record 130% yoy, and conventional memory and HBM pricing expectations have largely reset and started to recover.

DoorDash (DASH) announced product and platform updates at Dash Forward 2026. GS sees DASH evolving from food delivery into a three-sided local commerce platform, balancing growth investment against margin, including AI and autonomy investments (DoorDash Air and Dot).

earnings_insights: Micron reported FY4Q revenue of $54.23 bn (vs GS $51.91 bn, Street $50.95 bn), non-GAAP EPS $33.42 reported (vs GS $32.54, Street $31.63) and non-GAAP gross margin 87.0% (vs Street 86.9%). DRAM revenue was $39.8 bn and NAND revenue $14.1 bn.

Micron FY1Q guidance (estimates for the coming quarter): revenue $61.5 bn at the midpoint (GS $57.70 bn, Street $57.57 bn), non-GAAP gross margin 86.25% (GS 88.1%, Street 87.4%), non-GAAP EPS $37.15-39.15 (GS $37.06, Street $35.81).

Accenture reported 4Q26 revenue of $18.68 bn (Street $18.04 bn, GS est $18.13 bn), EPS from continuing operations of $3.29 reported (Street $3.19, GS est $3.12), adjusted operating margin 15.3%, and new bookings of $22.7 bn (Street $19.90 bn).

Accenture guided FY27 adjusted EPS to $14.39-14.81 (Street $14.62, GS est $14.75) and constant-currency revenue growth of 3-6%. Guidance for 1Q27 is revenue of $18.95-19.60 bn (Street and GS $19.4 bn).
Synopsys long-term targets from Investor Day: FY30 EPS of $35.00 and 50% operating margin, above the Street.
GS cuts its Samsung 3Q26E operating profit estimate to W106tn from W112tn on KRW strength, in line with consensus. Its 2027-28 estimates are 8-17% above the Street.
